Stable primary key for the logical signal. Never reuse.

The other Signal Ids that observe one and the same real-world quantity: a sensor and its backup, a CON and a MON channel, the same bus voltage measured at several points, a measured and an estimated value. Test: one change in the world moves them all at once. Declared on every member of the group, each listing the others.
Name of what is measured or commanded.

What kind of interface the row is, which also fixes how Interfacing Equipment and Signal Owner relate. 

Measurement: state acquired by a component from sensing hardware, including crew levers, selectors and pushbuttons; Interfacing equipement to Owner.

Command: hardwired drive of an effector or safety device; Owner to Physical; Analog or Discrete.

Request: setpoint, enable or mode asked of another controller over a data bus; Owner to Interfacing Equipment; Digital.

Computed: value derived by its owner, defined as an intermediate and derived state from other inputs. Interfacing Equipment empty.

Power: electrical supply, Owner is the source and Interfacing Equipment the load; Interface Type says which network (Low Power 28 V or High Power 800 V). See the Signal Role philosophy section in README.
Short label for the signal.
Equipment the quantity belongs to.
System that owns the signal path / computation.
Extra instance dimensions not already implied by owner/physical. Bare UniqueIds only — not NAC-1.
Free-text connection or sensing technology note.

Physical interface kind. Drives the Analog / Discrete / Low Power / High Power topology links when Physical is not the Owner. Low Power is the 28 V supply network, High Power the 800 V traction network.
Allowed values: Digital; Analog; Discrete; Low Power; High Power

Description: Engineering unit when applicable.
Lower end of the functional range of the quantity itself: the smallest value the interface is expected to carry in service. Independent of how it is encoded on any bus.

Upper end of the functional range of the quantity itself. Aircraft pitch may be functionally limited to 45 deg while the bus encoding allows 90 deg; the 45 deg belongs here and the 90 deg on the allocation row.

The Signal Ids this value is produced from: inputs of a computation, or the upstream signal when an owner re-emits an intent it received (HICU forwarding an MBMS limit). Signal Ids only, semicolon separated - explain the calculation in Notes. Empty when the owner relays a value unchanged under the same Signal Id, and for protocol fields such as counters and CRCs. This is an interface document: do not record engineering analysis such as which measurement a command is tuned against.
